**Menu map**
- New page under *Menus > Menu map*. It shows the right-click menu for a file (pick a type: .txt, .png, .exe, .zip, .pdf or .mp3), a folder, the folder background, the desktop, a drive or the taskbar.
- Your Shell items are listed with their file and line. The items Windows and installed programs add are listed with who added them, for example *Windows* or *7-Zip*. To read them, Shell builds the menu off-screen for a sample file: no window or menu appears and nothing is run.
- Tags show what your rules do to each item: *Hidden*, *Moved to …*, *Renamed to …*, *May be hidden* when a rule depends on the selection, and *Shows only sometimes* for your items with conditions.
- Two views: *Outline*, a list with submenus you can expand, and *Nodes*, with each submenu in its own panel.
- Click an item to see where it comes from, when it shows and which rules change it.
- Hide, rename or move a Windows or program item. The app writes the rule to a new file, `imports/settings-app-map.nss`, and saves it with *Save* in the footer, after checking the config and taking a snapshot in *Backups*. Rules use the item's Windows id when Shell knows it, so they work in every language.
- Hide or rename one of your own items, or edit just its code in a small editor. Only that part of the file changes.
- Docs: [Menu map](https://abdullah-masood-05.github.io/Shell/app/menu-map/).

**Context Menus page**
- The rules made on the Menu map page are listed under `imports/settings-app-map.nss`, each with a switch, and the file appears as the module *Menu map*.

**For developers**
- `shell -config:tree <file> -context:<where> [-sample:<path>]` prints the menu for one place as JSON, with your items, Windows' items and the rules that change them. It is read-only and never shows a window. `scripts/check-menu-tree.ps1` runs it on the shipped config for every context.

**Fixed in beta.2**
- Ctrl+S saves on every page that has a Save button or the unsaved-changes footer, including Context Menus, Menu Builder and Open with. It only worked inside the code editors before.
